why_this_rate: Carried from the classes that measured it rather than fitted here. A shelf this far below half the rate is its analogue self whichever of the candidate rates is used, so this record cannot and need not say.

map.why: The window the gain class closed on, taken as it stands rather than refitted here. What is being asked is the section and not the law on the byte, and a gain refitted per type would let a first-order shelf borrow a second-order one's steepness by claiming more decibels.

chain.why_a_point_inside_a_range: The claim publishes this corner as the band that fits every record inside its own floor, and this is a point the fit landed on inside that band rather than the band's own value. An earlier reading called it a lower bound, because the deviation was still climbing where both band sets end; that was a first-order shelf whose half-gain point was not where its parameter said, and through the section this model names the deviation climbs on both sides. Moving this number anywhere inside the band changes no residual the claim reports by more than the records' own floors, which is what the band means, so it is left where the fit put it. The refuted second-order candidate beside this one still carries the older wording: its corner was not re-read, because it is refuted by where its worst band sits and not by where its corner is.
